**Asia pre-market reactions - 2026-11-03**

**TL;DR**

- **A tech rout and an oil rout hit Asia together.** Taiwan closed **-3.59%** and Korea **-3.59%** (KOSDAQ -4.08%) on the US chip selloff and an AI-capex funding scare, while Brent fell 7.6% on US-Iran peace-talk hopes and dragged Korean refiners down a second, separate track.
- **Hong Kong bucked it (+0.57%)** - but only because consumer, property and leisure names bid while the tech complex sold off; the divergence is intra-market, not a risk-on session.
- **Tokyo was closed for Culture Day**, so Japan has no same-session print - the Japan section below is the **2 Nov** close, clearly labelled.
- Biggest single-name move of the day: **Hanjin KAL (180640) +29.97% limit-up** on a control battle, not on the market theme.

**Japan (TSE) - CLOSED for Culture Day**

- `market_open_jp=FALSE` - Tokyo was shut on Tuesday 3 November (Culture Day). The screener therefore returns the **2 November** session, the last settled print (`_data_date_jp=2026-11-02`).
- Those rows are **not** today’s moves and are shown only as prior-session context for the 4 Nov open.
- Yahoo quote pages for 7735.T and 285A.T both label their close "November 2", confirming the session date.

- The 2 Nov print was already highly dispersed inside Japan: semiconductor equipment split hard (Tokyo Electron +5.16%, Lasertec +8.01% against SCREEN -18.96%, Kioxia -15.78%).
- The SOX then fell a further 3.37% on 2 Nov US time, so the 4 Nov Tokyo open is at risk of extending that split.

**Taiwan (TWSE + TPEX)**

- **Driver:** the US chip rout plus a slide in AI-spending sentiment. TSMC fell 1.50% to NT$2,295 and MediaTek 7.43% to NT$3,675, ASE 8.61%, Delta 6.27%,
- Hon Hai 2.19% (CNA) - the mega-caps were spared only because the weight of the loss sat in mid-caps.
- Dealers pointed at a 7th-steepest point fall ever, a weaker TWD and stop-loss and program selling. Turnover was NT$928.06bn against NT$799.69bn on Monday (CNA).

**Korea (KRX)**

- **Driver:** two shocks at once - the AI-capex and tech-funding scare (ChosunBiz: Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, SK Square and Samsung Electro-Mechanics all down ~5%) and an oil collapse.
- Brent settled at $104.77 (-7.63%) and WTI at $96.46 (-7.36%) as US-Iran peace talks and a possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz repriced supply risk;
- refiners were sold for inventory-valuation losses.
